Hill of Gareb
GAY-reb
proper noun
Hebrew Gareb, perhaps “scabby” or “leprous,” a common or unclean place; a hill near Jerusalem named in the promise of the city’s restoration.

📖 Biblical Definition

In the great chapter of the new covenant, where the LORD promises to write His law in the inward parts and to remember sin no more, He adds a word of the city’s rebuilding: “And the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath” (Jer 31:39). Gareb bears a name that speaks of scab or leprosy, a mean and unclean spot on the edge of the holy city; yet the measuring line of promise is stretched out over it, and it is drawn within the compass of what shall be holy unto the LORD. The verse following declares that the whole valley, even the place of dead bodies and ashes, shall be holy, and shall not be plucked up nor thrown down any more for ever. Gareb preaches the sanctifying of the common and the cleansing of the unclean. What was scabbed and cast to the outskirts is measured into the city of God. So the covenant of grace takes the leprous sinner, the outcast, the place of ashes, and draws the line of holiness about him, saying he shall not be plucked up any more for ever. Here is the perseverance of the saints written upon a hill: not measured for a season, but compassed into a holiness that abides, a city whose builder and maker is God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A hill near Jerusalem, its name suggesting the scabbed or unclean, drawn within the measuring line of the promised holy city (Jer 31:39); a figure of the common made holy and kept for ever.

HILL OF GAREB, a height near Jerusalem named in Jeremiah’s promise.

Its name suggests the scabbed, leprous, or unclean.

The measuring line of restoration goes forth upon it (Jer 31:39).

It is compassed within what shall be holy unto the LORD.

A figure of the common cleansed and kept, not plucked up for ever.

📖 Key Scripture

Jer 31:39 — "And the measuring line shall yet go forth over against it upon the hill Gareb, and shall compass about to Goath."

Heb 11:16 — "But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city."

Heb 13:14 — "For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come."

Psa 46:4 — "There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

An unclean hill drawn into the promised holy city; it recovers the sanctifying grace that makes the common holy and keeps it for ever.

expand to see more

An obscure hill named once in prophecy stirs no controversy in the present age. What deserves recovery is not a quarrel but a comfort: that the LORD measures the unclean and the outcast into His holy city.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the sanctifying grace of the new covenant, which draws the scabbed and common within the compass of holiness and secures it there. The line goes forth upon Gareb, and the word is that nothing shall be plucked up nor thrown down any more for ever. What grace measures in, grace keeps: the outcast becomes the abiding citizen of the city of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Gareb is linked to a root meaning scab or itch, hence a leprous or unclean place; the very name magnifies the grace that makes it holy.

expand to see more

Gareb — from a root meaning scab, itch, or leprosy.

Hence a mean or unclean place on the city’s edge.

Named once, in the promise of Jerusalem’s rebuilding (Jer 31:39).

The measuring line is compassed from it about to Goath.

A name of uncleanness swallowed up in a word of holiness.

Usage

"The measuring line shall go forth upon the hill Gareb."

"Gareb was a mean place drawn into the holy city."

"From Gareb the line compassed about to Goath."
